statusDetail: Coverage complete: all 58 registered checks received conclusive outcomes across six representative route archetypes plus a missing-route recovery test.

page.notes: Public government admissions directory with Angular client rendering. Six representative routes cover landing, filter/list, chooser, search/list, notifications and contact. External counselling sites, sign-in, destructive/account flows and downstream application submission were not covered because they cross to separate origins or were disabled.

findings.summary: The site does not follow the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark the screenshot remains white and the computed body colors remain rgb(255,255,255) on rgb(33,37,41).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface and text tokens, with tested media/content contrast.

findings.summary: An animation continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reports one running animation with a 1000 ms duration while matchMedia(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) is true.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential carousel/transition animation and auto-advance inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: SPA route changes have no directional or continuity transition.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition signal, while the audited Home, Institutes, OR-CR and Counsellings routes replace the main view in the Angular shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for route content, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-position-aware navigation or progress cue.
findings.evidence: The mobile home is 5,284 CSS pixels tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or progress/position affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained scroll-aware cue such as a shrinking header, back-to-top action, or section progress where it aids orientation.

findings.summary: Components adapt only through global layout rules, not their own containers.
findings.evidence: The responsive mobile screenshots render without overflow, but CSS inspection found no @container or container-type signal across reused cards and filters.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reused counselling cards and filter modules that appear in different widths.

findings.summary: Several controls are too small and some focusable controls have no accessible name.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe found 11×11 carousel dots, a 20×20 Pause target, many 14–23 px-high links, and three unnamed focusable controls; Lighthouse target-size also failed eight targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24×24 CSS px targets with adequate spacing (prefer 44×44 for primary touch controls), visible focus, and names for icon/custom controls.

findings.summary: Initial content is slow to become visible.
findings.evidence: The trace measured FCP/LCP at 3,478.53 ms and load end at 4,036.14 ms; Lighthouse performance scored 0.45.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content, shorten critical chains, remove duplicated blocking libraries, and defer non-critical translation/analytics work.

findings.summary: Startup scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded two long tasks (126.52 ms and 101.61 ms) and 128.13 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up startup work and defer or conditionally load non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: The critical path includes blocking legacy scripts and oversized, unsized images.
findings.evidence: HAR/DOM evidence confirms parser-inserted non-deferred jQuery, Popper, Bootstrap, and a second jQuery; 1.54 MB transfers include a 316 KB banner, while all 28 images lack both dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate jQuery, defer non-critical scripts, reserve image space, and optimize/preload only the true LCP asset.

findings.summary: The page ships duplicate and legacy JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM lists two jQuery files plus ES2015 and ES5 bundle variants; Lighthouse flags missing source maps for a large first-party bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate libraries, verify nomodule/module delivery, tree-shake bundles, and publish production source maps securely.

findings.summary: Key images and controls lack accessible alternatives.
findings.evidence: The images audit found 21 of 28 images without alt; Lighthouse failed image-alt (7 rendered nodes) and button-name (2 nodes), and the Counsellings stream select has no label.
findings.suggestedFix: Add context-appropriate alt text or empty alt for decoration, label the select, and name all icon buttons.

findings.summary: Text and controls repeatedly fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed 24 nodes on the landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace low-contrast gray/blue combinations with tokens meeting WCAG AA in every theme and state.

findings.summary: Heading structure and focus semantics are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; several non-home routes expose no meaningful page heading, and the focus probe found unnamed controls and inputs whose computed outline is none.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each route a logical H1-led hierarchy and use :focus-visible styles that remain visible on every control.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console and reported seven logged browser errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve failed requests and runtime/third-party errors, and keep production console monitoring clean.

findings.summary: Image sizing and aspect-ratio handling are unsound.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports all 28 images missing width/height; Lighthouse also failed image-aspect-ratio for one rendered image.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and preserve natural aspect ratios in CSS.

findings.summary: Production debugging and browser hygiene have unresolved issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports two DevTools Inspector issues and a missing source map for a large first-party JavaScript bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: Review DevTools Issues, update stale libraries, and provide valid source maps through an access-controlled release pipeline.

findings.summary: Every audited route uses a generic title and has no meta description.
findings.evidence: Rendered metadata reports title “Admissions” and no description; Lighthouse fails meta-description, and route probes show the same title across six archetypes.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate unique route-specific titles and concise meta descriptions reflecting each visible task.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are incomplete and nonexistent routes return a success shell.
findings.evidence: No canonical was found; /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml return 404; an application nonexistent route returns HTTP 200.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve accurate 404 status codes, publish robots.txt and sitemap.xml, and add self-referencing canonicals for public routes.

findings.summary: The public admissions entity has no structured or share-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite and relevant page-level schema.org JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter preview metadata.

findings.summary: Session cookies and the CSP are not securely hardened.
findings.evidence: CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; ASP.NET_SessionId lacks Secure, and another session cookie lacks HttpOnly and uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Harden CSP with nonces/hashes and no unsafe-eval, and set Secure, HttpOnly, and the narrowest workable SameSite value on session cookies.

findings.summary: The public portal loads tracking and translation third parties by default.
findings.evidence: Tracker/HAR evidence finds four third-party origins, Google Tag Manager, seven third-party requests and 280,624 third-party bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Document the data purpose, minimize analytics, defer translation resources until needed, and gate non-essential tracking on valid consent where required.

findings.summary: Important browser-enforced security policies are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence finds no HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy after staged testing.

findings.summary: All core public content disappears without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability evidence fetched 783 bytes of raw HTML with zero visible text/content tokens, 0% rendered-word coverage, no title or H1, and a blank crawler screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render or pre-render route content and keep core links/forms functional as progressive HTML enhancements.

findings.summary: Unknown routes resolve to a misleading successful application shell.
findings.evidence: A fetch of /admiss/admissions/definitely-missing-web-uplift returned HTTP 200 with the generic Admissions shell instead of a 404 recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Return the correct status and render a branded, actionable not-found page with links back to admissions tasks.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bandwidth.
findings.evidence: The page transfers 733,872 image bytes; 13 images use legacy formats, 10 below-fold images are not lazy, five are oversized, and six responsive candidates lack srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert raster assets to AVIF/WebP, emit responsive sources, lazy-load below-fold media, and right-size logos and banners.

findings.summary: Third-party and decorative bytes are disproportionate for a mostly informational page.
findings.evidence: The 1.54 MB load includes 280,624 third-party bytes and a 316,400-byte banner; translation resources are loaded twice in the script list.
findings.suggestedFix: Load translation once and on demand, remove redundant third parties, and compress/defer decorative media.
